root_cause.text: The `mfd_of_node_list` global linked list was accessed and modified without any mutual exclusion mechanism, creating a race condition where concurrent list operations from multiple threads could corrupt the list structure or cause use-after-free crashes.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `static DEFINE_MUTEX(mfd_of_node_mutex)` and wraps all four locations where `mfd_of_node_list` is accessed or modified with `scoped_guard(mutex, &mfd_of_node_mutex)`. The original code at lines 107-109, 131, 291-296, and 367-372 performed unprotected list traversals, insertions, and deletions on a global list that could be accessed concurrently from different code paths (device matching, device addition, and device removal), violating the kernel's requirement that "manipulating a list in the kernel isn't safe without some sort of mutual exclusion" as stated in the commit message.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add mutex synchronization primitive to protect the mfd_of_node_list from concurrent access race conditions.
intent_record.what: Added a static mutex declaration `static DEFINE_MUTEX(mfd_of_node_mutex);` immediately after the existing `static LIST_HEAD(mfd_of_node_list);` declaration.
intent_record.how: This introduces a mutex lock that will protect concurrent access to the `mfd_of_node_list` linked list. Without this mutex, simultaneous read/write operations on the list from different threads could cause data corruption or race conditions. The mutex enables safe synchronization of list operations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add mutex protection around the mfd_of_node_list traversal to prevent concurrent access race conditions.
intent_record.what: Wrapped the existing list_for_each_entry loop and its conditional check with a scoped_guard(mutex, &mfd_of_node_mutex) block, adding mutex locking around the critical section that accesses mfd_of_node_list.
intent_record.how: This change adds automatic mutex acquisition and release around the list traversal that checks if an OF node has already been allocated. The scoped_guard macro ensures the mutex is held for the duration of the block and automatically released when exiting, preventing race conditions where multiple threads could simultaneously check and modify the mfd_of_node_list.

The scoped_guard macro automatically acquires the mutex at the start of the guarded block and releases it at the end, preventing race conditions where concurrent threads could corrupt the list structure during insertion.
